tagline: A higher-quality natural voice for every app — faster on a graphics chip, no key, no cloud.
description:
This is a voice other apps can use. Install it, keep it in your Providers folder, and assign it to Text → speech in Settings → AI models. From then on every app that asks GifOS to speak — Reader, games, anything that talks — is answered by this app, entirely on your device.

The voice is Kokoro (Apache-2.0), a natural-sounding model with eight voices: Heart, Bella, Nicole, Sarah, Michael, Fenrir, Emma and George. It also answers to the familiar cloud names (nova, shimmer, fable, echo, onyx, alloy), so anything written for a cloud voice works unchanged.

GRAPHICS CHIP WHEN YOU HAVE ONE. This voice runs faster on a computer with a graphics chip, and falls back to the processor where there isn't one. Same voice either way; a real graphics chip just makes it think faster. Its smaller sibling, Offline Neural Text to Speech, stays the always-on-the-processor option — pick whichever you prefer in Settings.

WHAT IT COSTS, PLAINLY. The engine rides inside the app, but the 163 MB voice is downloaded once, checked against a fingerprint baked into the app, and kept on your device. Because it is a natural-sounding model it thinks before it speaks: it generates a passage of audio before that passage can start playing, so there is a pause at the beginning of each one — shorter on a graphics chip, longer on the processor, and longer the more text it is handed at once.

Once the voice is on your device it never asks the network again. The app itself cannot reach the network, so nothing you ask it to say can leave this device.
author: GifOS
